claims.text: Near-equiatomic NiTi exhibits increasing critical stress for plastic flow as testing temperature rises.
Thermally activated phase transformations inhibit dislocation slip in near-equiatomic NiTi.
The proposed alloy contains approximately 50 at% Ni and 50 at% Ti.
The proposed initial state is produced by solution annealing at approximately 800°C for 30 minutes followed by water quenching.
Testing temperature is to be increased incrementally from room temperature to approximately 100°C under tensile loading.
Tests are to use a constant strain rate and a roughly 10-minute soak at each temperature.
NiTi undergoes reversible B2-to-B19' and B19'-to-B2 phase transformations.
The reversible B2↔B19' transformations influence the ease of dislocation motion.
Elevated temperature stabilizes the austenite phase in NiTi.
Austenite stabilization increases the applied stress required to induce martensite.
Stress-induced martensite formation is followed by plastic flow.
Flow stress will increase monotonically with temperature up to approximately 100°C.
Higher temperatures produce greater resistance to plastic deformation.
Room-temperature NiTi without thermal cycling has a lower critical stress for slip than NiTi tested at higher temperatures.
Significant deviation of Ni content from 50 at% can markedly alter transformation behavior and stress response.
Testing above approximately 100°C can markedly alter transformation behavior and stress response.
Minor compositional shifts and processing conditions can change the transformation temperatures and stress levels.
